aws.a.accessanalyzer.region_active.description: For an account and Region, fails if no analyzer is declared or any declared analyzer is not ACTIVE. This all-analyzers status predicate does not establish that an external-access analyzer exists; analyzer type and zone of trust are not checked. Missing inventory is UNKNOWN.
aws.a.accessanalyzer.region_active.pass_when: PASS when the region has one or more analyzers and every one has status ACTIVE.
aws.a.accessanalyzer.region_active.fail_when: FAIL when the region has no analyzers, or at least one analyzer is CREATING, DISABLED or FAILED.

aws.a.accessanalyzer.region_present.description: Scope-level check per account/region that FAILs when the completely collected IAM Access Analyzer inventory for that region contains no analyzer at all. Without an analyzer, nobody is alerted when a bucket, KMS key, role trust policy or other resource policy starts granting access to external or public principals.
evaluated: access_analyzer[].arn (count of analyzers in the account/region scope)
aws.a.accessanalyzer.region_present.pass_when: PASS when at least one Access Analyzer is declared in the region, regardless of its status.
aws.a.accessanalyzer.region_present.fail_when: FAIL when the region's analyzer inventory was collected successfully and is empty.

aws.a.account.organization_member.description: Account-configuration check that FAILs when the Organizations lookup proves the account has no organization (DescribeOrganization returned an empty/absent result). A standalone account sits outside SCP guardrails, centralized CloudTrail/GuardDuty/Config delegation and consolidated governance, so preventive and detective controls must be maintained per account.
aws.a.account.organization_member.pass_when: PASS when an OrganizationId starting with 'o-' is reported for the account.
aws.a.account.organization_member.fail_when: FAIL when the collected Organization fact is explicitly empty/absent (account not in an organization).

aws.a.account.security_contact_present.description: Account-configuration check that FAILs when no security alternate contact is registered for the account (contact proven absent or NamePresent false) in the aws or aws-cn partitions. Without a security contact, AWS Trust & Safety abuse and compromise notifications go only to the root email, which may be unmonitored, delaying incident response.
aws.a.account.security_contact_present.pass_when: PASS when the SECURITY alternate contact exists and has a name.
aws.a.account.security_contact_present.fail_when: FAIL when the SECURITY alternate contact is proven absent or has no name.

aws.a.cloudtrail.bucket_access_logging.description: For every CloudTrail trail, joins the trail's S3BucketName to the same-account bucket inventory and FAILs when that destination bucket has no server access logging (no Logging.LoggingEnabled.TargetBucket). Without access logs on the log bucket, reads, deletions or tampering with the CloudTrail log files themselves leave no audit record.
aws.a.cloudtrail.bucket_access_logging.pass_when: PASS when the joined trail bucket has LoggingEnabled with a non-empty TargetBucket.
aws.a.cloudtrail.bucket_access_logging.fail_when: FAIL when the joined trail bucket's logging configuration was collected and has no LoggingEnabled block or an empty target.

aws.a.cloudtrail.bucket_mfa_delete.description: For CloudTrail trails that are currently logging, joins the destination S3 bucket from the same-account inventory and FAILs when its versioning configuration does not report MFADelete=Enabled. Without MFA Delete, anyone with the right S3 permissions (including a compromised principal) can permanently delete log object versions or suspend versioning to erase audit evidence.
aws.a.cloudtrail.bucket_mfa_delete.pass_when: PASS when the logging trail's in-account bucket reports MFADelete Enabled.
aws.a.cloudtrail.bucket_mfa_delete.fail_when: FAIL when the bucket reports MFADelete Disabled, or its versioning was collected without any MFADelete value.
aws.a.cloudtrail.bucket_mfa_delete.not_applicable_when: NOT_APPLICABLE when Status.IsLogging is false; an out-of-scope destination returns MANUAL.

aws.a.cloudtrail.cloudwatch_delivery_24h.description: Checks the latest CloudTrail delivery to CloudWatch Logs against the snapshot capture clock. A delivery timestamp in the future is UNKNOWN; a timestamp older than 24 hours fails; a successfully collected status without a delivery timestamp also fails. Missing or malformed required status or clock evidence is UNKNOWN.
aws.a.cloudtrail.cloudwatch_delivery_24h.pass_when: The latest delivery timestamp is timezone-aware and between capture time minus 24 hours and capture time, inclusive.
aws.a.cloudtrail.cloudwatch_delivery_24h.fail_when: The latest delivery is more than 24 hours old, or a collected status has no delivery timestamp.

aws.a.cloudtrail.home_bucket_access_logg.description: Evaluated only for a trail in its home region: joins its S3 destination to the complete same-account bucket inventory and FAILs when the bucket's logging configuration was collected without LoggingEnabled. Missing access logging on the trail bucket means access to and deletion of CloudTrail log files is not itself recorded.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_bucket_access_logg.pass_when: PASS when the joined in-account destination bucket has a LoggingEnabled block.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_bucket_access_logg.fail_when: FAIL when the joined bucket's logging was collected and no LoggingEnabled block exists.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_bucket_access_logg.not_applicable_when: Trail row is a shadow copy outside its home region, or the destination bucket is not in the account bucket inventory (inner join emits nothing).

aws.a.cloudtrail.home_bucket_mfa_join.description: For home-region trails, FAILs when the trail declares no S3BucketName, when the named bucket cannot be found in the complete same-account bucket inventory, or when the joined bucket does not report MFADelete Enabled. It requires MFA Delete to be provably verified on the log destination, since without it log versions can be permanently removed by a compromised principal.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_bucket_mfa_join.pass_when: PASS when the home-region trail's destination bucket is in the account inventory and reports MFADelete Enabled.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_bucket_mfa_join.fail_when: FAIL when no destination bucket is declared, the bucket is missing from the account inventory, or MFADelete is Disabled/not reported.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_bucket_mfa_join.not_applicable_when: Trail row is outside its home region.

aws.a.cloudtrail.home_cloudwatch_date.description: For home-region trails (single or multi-region), FAILs when no CloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn integration is declared, when no CloudWatch delivery time is reported, or when the last delivery is not after 00:00 UTC of the day before the capture date. This flags trails that are not feeding CloudWatch Logs, which prevents real-time alarms on root use, IAM changes and other CIS monitoring metrics.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_cloudwatch_date.pass_when: PASS when a log group ARN is declared and the latest delivery is later than midnight UTC of the previous captured day.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_cloudwatch_date.fail_when: FAIL when no log group integration, no delivery time, or a delivery at or before the previous-day midnight cutoff.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_cloudwatch_date.not_applicable_when: Trail row is outside its home region.

aws.a.cloudtrail.home_kms_encryption.description: For home-region CloudTrail trails, FAILs when the trail has an empty KmsKeyId, meaning log files are stored with only default S3-managed encryption. Without SSE-KMS, anyone with S3 read on the bucket can read the logs, and you lose the extra key-policy access control and key-usage audit trail.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_kms_encryption.pass_when: PASS when the trail declares a non-empty KmsKeyId.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_kms_encryption.fail_when: FAIL when the trail's KmsKeyId is empty.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_kms_encryption.not_applicable_when: Trail row is outside its home region.

aws.a.cloudtrail.home_logging_with_insig.description: For home-region trails, FAILs when the trail is not logging (Status.IsLogging false) or when it has no Insights selectors configured. This combines two gaps: a stopped trail records nothing, and a logging trail without ApiCallRate/ApiErrorRate Insights will not surface anomalous API-volume spikes typical of credential abuse.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_logging_with_insig.pass_when: PASS when the home-region trail is logging and has at least one Insights selector.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_logging_with_insig.fail_when: FAIL when the trail is not logging, or it is logging with no Insights selectors.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_logging_with_insig.not_applicable_when: Trail row is outside its home region.

aws.a.cloudtrail.home_multiregion_cloudw.description: Same CloudWatch freshness test as the home-region variant but restricted to multi-region trails: FAILs when a home-region multi-region trail has no CloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn, no delivery time, or a last delivery at or before 00:00 UTC of the previous captured day. An account-wide trail not streaming to CloudWatch leaves every region without real-time API alarming.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_multiregion_cloudw.pass_when: PASS when the multi-region trail declares a log group and delivered after the previous-day UTC midnight cutoff.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_multiregion_cloudw.fail_when: FAIL when the multi-region trail has no log group, no delivery time, or a stale delivery.
aws.a.cloudtrail.home_multiregion_cloudw.not_applicable_when: Trail row is outside its home region or the trail is not multi-region.

aws.a.cloudtrail.insights_logging_trail.description: For CloudTrail trails that are actively logging, FAILs when no Insights selectors are configured (selector list empty or proven absent). Without CloudTrail Insights, unusual write-API call rates or error rates, common during automated attacks or misused credentials, are not detected.
aws.a.cloudtrail.insights_logging_trail.pass_when: PASS when the logging trail has one or more Insights selectors.
aws.a.cloudtrail.insights_logging_trail.fail_when: FAIL when the logging trail has an empty or absent Insights selector configuration.

aws.a.cloudtrail.joined_bucket_declared_.description: For each trail, joins its S3 destination to the same-account bucket inventory and FAILs when the bucket ACL grants the global AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers groups, or when the bucket policy has an Allow statement with Principal '*' (or AWS '*'). A publicly readable or writable CloudTrail bucket exposes the full API activity history of the account and lets outsiders tamper with it.
aws.a.cloudtrail.joined_bucket_declared_.pass_when: PASS when the joined bucket has no AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers ACL grants and no Allow statement for a wildcard principal.
aws.a.cloudtrail.joined_bucket_declared_.fail_when: FAIL when the ACL grants a global public group, or the policy allows Principal '*' (conditions, denies and Block Public Access are not considered).
aws.a.cloudtrail.joined_bucket_declared_.not_applicable_when: Destination bucket is not in the complete same-account bucket inventory.

aws.a.cloudwatch.agentcore_data_protecti.description: For CloudWatch log groups whose name starts with /aws/bedrock-agentcore/ or /aws/vendedlogs/bedrock-agentcore/, FAILs when dataProtectionStatus is not ACTIVATED and the group does not inherit ACCOUNT_DATA_PROTECTION. AgentCore agent logs can carry prompts, tool outputs and user PII or secrets, and without a data protection policy those values are stored and readable in clear text.
aws.a.cloudwatch.agentcore_data_protecti.pass_when: PASS when the AgentCore log group has data protection ACTIVATED or inherits account-level data protection.
aws.a.cloudwatch.agentcore_data_protecti.fail_when: FAIL when the AgentCore log group has no active data protection and no inherited account data protection policy.
aws.a.cloudwatch.agentcore_data_protecti.not_applicable_when: Log group name does not start with a default AgentCore prefix.

aws.a.cloudwatch.alarm_actions_enabled.description: For each CloudWatch metric alarm, FAILs when ActionsEnabled is false. With actions disabled the alarm still changes state but sends no SNS notification, Auto Scaling or remediation action, so security and availability alarms silently fail to alert anyone.

aws.a.cloudwatch.alarm_state_actions.description: For each CloudWatch alarm, FAILs when the AlarmActions list (actions executed on transition to ALARM) is empty. An alarm with no ALARM-state target never notifies or triggers a response when the monitored condition, such as a CIS security metric filter, fires.
aws.a.cloudwatch.alarm_state_actions.pass_when: PASS when alarmActions contains at least one action ARN.

aws.a.cloudwatch.any_state_actions.description: For each CloudWatch alarm, FAILs only when AlarmActions, OKActions and InsufficientDataActions are all empty. Such an alarm is purely cosmetic: no state transition reaches any notification or automation target.
aws.a.cloudwatch.any_state_actions.pass_when: PASS when at least one action is configured in any of the three alarm states.
aws.a.cloudwatch.any_state_actions.fail_when: FAIL when All three action lists are empty.

aws.a.cloudwatch.cross_account_role_abse.description: Scope-level check that FAILs when the account's IAM role inventory contains a role named exactly CloudWatch-CrossAccountSharingRole. That role lets another account read this account's CloudWatch metrics, dashboards and alarms (and possibly logs), so its presence is a cross-account data-sharing path that must be justified.
aws.a.cloudwatch.cross_account_role_abse.pass_when: PASS when no IAM role named CloudWatch-CrossAccountSharingRole exists in the account.
aws.a.cloudwatch.cross_account_role_abse.fail_when: FAIL when a role named CloudWatch-CrossAccountSharingRole exists (its trust policy is not evaluated).

aws.a.cloudwatch.finite_retention_365.description: For each CloudWatch log group, FAILs when retentionInDays is absent (Never Expire) or below 365. This is stricter than an 'at least a year' test: it requires an explicit retention of 365 days or more, so groups that keep logs forever are flagged for unmanaged growth and indefinite retention of possibly sensitive data.
aws.a.cloudwatch.finite_retention_365.pass_when: PASS when retentionInDays is explicitly set to 365 or more.
aws.a.cloudwatch.finite_retention_365.fail_when: FAIL when retentionInDays is not set (never expire) or is less than 365.

aws.a.cloudwatch.log_kms_encryption.description: For each CloudWatch log group, FAILs when no kmsKeyId is associated (the DescribeLogGroups response proves the field is absent). Without a customer KMS key, log data is protected only by service-owned keys, so key-policy based access separation, revocation and key-usage auditing are not available for potentially sensitive logs.
aws.a.cloudwatch.log_kms_encryption.pass_when: PASS when the log group has a non-empty kmsKeyId.
aws.a.cloudwatch.log_kms_encryption.fail_when: FAIL when the log group has no associated KMS key.

aws.a.cloudwatch.log_retention_at_least_.description: For each CloudWatch log group, FAILs when retentionInDays is set to fewer than 365 days; a group with no retention (Never Expire) passes. Short retention destroys audit and forensic evidence before most incidents are discovered or compliance look-back periods end.
aws.a.cloudwatch.log_retention_at_least_.pass_when: PASS when retentionInDays is absent (never expire) or 365 or more.
aws.a.cloudwatch.log_retention_at_least_.fail_when: FAIL when retentionInDays is a positive value below 365.

aws.a.config.region_recorder_enabled.description: Scope-level check per account/region that FAILs when no AWS Config configuration recorder exists, or when any recorder's matching status entry shows recording=false or lastStatus=Failure. Without a working recorder, configuration changes are not captured, Config rules cannot evaluate, and resource history needed for investigations is missing.
aws.a.config.region_recorder_enabled.pass_when: PASS when Every recorder in the region is recording and none reports lastStatus Failure (Pending is accepted).
aws.a.config.region_recorder_enabled.fail_when: FAIL when the region has no recorder, or a recorder is not recording or reports lastStatus Failure.

aws.a.guardduty.region_enabled.description: Scope-level check per account/region that FAILs when no GuardDuty detector exists in the region or the single detector's status is DISABLED. Without GuardDuty, threat detection for credential exfiltration, crypto-mining, malicious IP traffic and anomalous API calls is absent in that region, which attackers often target precisely because it is unused.
aws.a.guardduty.region_enabled.pass_when: PASS when exactly one detector exists in the region and its status is ENABLED.
aws.a.guardduty.region_enabled.fail_when: FAIL when the region has no detector or the detector status is DISABLED.

aws.a.iam.active_key_age_90.description: For each IAM access key with Status Active, FAILs when its CreateDate is on or before the cutoff of 00:00 UTC of the capture date minus 90 days. Long-lived static keys keep accumulating exposure (in code, CI logs, laptops) and a leaked old key stays valid until rotated.
aws.a.iam.active_key_age_90.pass_when: PASS when the active key was created after the 90-day cutoff.
aws.a.iam.active_key_age_90.fail_when: FAIL when the active key was created at or before the 90-day cutoff.

aws.a.iam.attached_policy_no_star_star.description: For IAM managed policies that are attached to at least one principal (AttachmentCount > 0), inspects the default policy version and FAILs when any Allow statement combines Resource '*' with Action '*' or '*:*'. Such a customer-managed policy grants full administrator rights to every principal it is attached to.
aws.a.iam.attached_policy_no_star_star.pass_when: PASS when no Allow statement in the default version has both '*' action and '*' resource.
aws.a.iam.attached_policy_no_star_star.fail_when: FAIL when a customer-managed attached policy's default version has an Allow '*'/'*:*' on Resource '*' (conditions are not considered).
aws.a.iam.attached_policy_no_star_star.not_applicable_when: NOT_APPLICABLE when AttachmentCount is zero; an AWS-managed policy with a matching statement returns MANUAL.

aws.a.iam.console_key_created_at_setup.description: For a console-enabled IAM user, the credential report's access_key_1_last_rotated records creation or last change of the current key, not first-key history. A present timestamp yields UNKNOWN for the historical initial-setup criterion. No current first key, or no console password, passes the observed predicate.
aws.a.iam.console_key_created_at_setup.pass_when: The user has no console password or no current first access key.
aws.a.iam.console_key_created_at_setup.fail_when: This evaluator does not emit FAIL from last-rotated time; historical initial creation requires independent evidence.

aws.a.iam.group_no_cloudshell_full_acces.description: For each IAM group, FAILs when its AttachedManagedPolicies directly include arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AWSCloudShellFullAccess. That policy gives every member unrestricted CloudShell use, including file upload/download, which can be used to exfiltrate data or stage tooling inside the account.
aws.a.iam.group_no_cloudshell_full_acces.pass_when: PASS when the group has no direct AWSCloudShellFullAccess attachment.
aws.a.iam.group_no_cloudshell_full_acces.fail_when: FAIL when AWSCloudShellFullAccess is attached directly to the group.

aws.a.iam.password_policy_expiry_at_most.description: Account-scope check of the IAM account password policy that FAILs when no password policy is configured, or when PasswordPolicy.MaxPasswordAge is greater than 90 days. Passwords that never expire, or expire only after a long time, stay usable for longer after they leak.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_expiry_at_most.pass_when: PASS when a password policy exists and MaxPasswordAge is 90 days or less.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_expiry_at_most.fail_when: FAIL when no account password policy exists, or MaxPasswordAge is greater than 90 days.

aws.a.iam.password_policy_lowercase.description: Account-scope check of the IAM account password policy that FAILs when no password policy is configured, or when PasswordPolicy.RequireLowercaseCharacters is false. Without a lowercase requirement, users can choose passwords with fewer character classes, which are easier to guess or brute-force.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_lowercase.pass_when: PASS when a password policy exists and RequireLowercaseCharacters is true.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_lowercase.fail_when: FAIL when no account password policy exists, or RequireLowercaseCharacters is false.

aws.a.iam.password_policy_minimum_length.description: Account-scope check of the IAM account password policy that FAILs when no password policy is configured, or when PasswordPolicy.MinimumPasswordLength is 13 or less. Short IAM console passwords are much easier to brute-force or crack offline.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_minimum_length.pass_when: PASS when a password policy exists and MinimumPasswordLength is 14 or more.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_minimum_length.fail_when: FAIL when no account password policy exists, or MinimumPasswordLength is 13 or less.

aws.a.iam.password_policy_numbers.description: Account-scope check of the IAM account password policy that FAILs when no password policy is configured, or when PasswordPolicy.RequireNumbers is false. Without a digit requirement, users can pick weaker dictionary-style passwords.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_numbers.pass_when: PASS when a password policy exists and RequireNumbers is true.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_numbers.fail_when: FAIL when no account password policy exists, or RequireNumbers is false.

aws.a.iam.password_policy_reuse_at_least.description: Account-scope check of the IAM account password policy that FAILs when no password policy is configured, or when PasswordPolicy.PasswordReusePrevention is below 24. Low reuse prevention lets users switch back to previously compromised passwords.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_reuse_at_least.pass_when: PASS when a password policy exists and PasswordReusePrevention is 24 or more.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_reuse_at_least.fail_when: FAIL when no account password policy exists, or PasswordReusePrevention is below 24.

aws.a.iam.password_policy_strong_min_len.description: Account-scope composite check that FAILs unless the IAM password policy exists and at the same time requires a minimum length of 14 or more, lowercase, uppercase, numbers and symbols, PasswordReusePrevention of 24 or more and MaxPasswordAge of 90 days or less. Any one missing control weakens IAM console passwords against guessing, reuse of leaked passwords or indefinite validity.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_strong_min_len.pass_when: PASS when All seven requirements (length 14 or more, four character classes, reuse 24 or more, max age 90 or less) are met.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_strong_min_len.fail_when: FAIL when the policy is absent or any one of the seven requirements is not met.

aws.a.iam.password_policy_strong_min_len.description: Account-scope composite check that FAILs unless the IAM password policy exists, MinimumPasswordLength is at least 8, and lowercase, uppercase, number and symbol characters are all required. This is a baseline-complexity test (no reuse or expiry requirement) to stop trivially guessable console passwords.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_strong_min_len.pass_when: PASS when minimum length is 8 or more and all four character-class requirements are true.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_strong_min_len.fail_when: FAIL when the policy is absent, length is below 8, or any character-class requirement is false.

aws.a.iam.password_policy_symbols.description: Account-scope check of the IAM account password policy that FAILs when no password policy is configured, or when PasswordPolicy.RequireSymbols is false. Without a symbol requirement, the search space for brute-forcing is smaller.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_symbols.pass_when: PASS when a password policy exists and RequireSymbols is true.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_symbols.fail_when: FAIL when no account password policy exists, or RequireSymbols is false.

aws.a.iam.password_policy_uppercase.description: Account-scope check of the IAM account password policy that FAILs when no password policy is configured, or when PasswordPolicy.RequireUppercaseCharacters is false. Without an uppercase requirement, users can choose all-lowercase passwords that are easier to guess.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_uppercase.pass_when: PASS when a password policy exists and RequireUppercaseCharacters is true.
aws.a.iam.password_policy_uppercase.fail_when: FAIL when no account password policy exists, or RequireUppercaseCharacters is false.

aws.a.iam.report_all_mfa.description: For every IAM credential-report row (including users without console passwords), FAILs when mfa_active is false. Principals without any MFA device rely on a single factor, so a stolen password or phished session leads directly to account access.

aws.a.iam.report_console_mfa.description: For IAM credential-report rows, FAILs when password_enabled is true but mfa_active is false, i.e. a console-login identity without MFA. Console users without MFA can be taken over with only a guessed, reused or phished password.
aws.a.iam.report_console_mfa.pass_when: PASS when the identity has no console password or has MFA active.
aws.a.iam.report_console_mfa.fail_when: FAIL when the identity has a console password and no active MFA device.

aws.a.iam.role_no_cloudshell_full_access.description: For each IAM role, FAILs when AWSCloudShellFullAccess is in its directly attached managed policies. Any principal that can assume the role gets full CloudShell access, including data transfer in and out of the shell environment.
aws.a.iam.role_no_cloudshell_full_access.pass_when: PASS when the role has no direct AWSCloudShellFullAccess attachment.
aws.a.iam.role_no_cloudshell_full_access.fail_when: FAIL when AWSCloudShellFullAccess is attached directly to the role.

aws.a.iam.root_console_summary_mfa.description: Using the IAM account summary, FAILs when the root user has a console password (AccountPasswordPresent=1) and AccountMFAEnabled=0. A root user with a password and no MFA can be fully compromised by anyone who obtains the root email password, with unrestricted control of the account.
aws.a.iam.root_console_summary_mfa.pass_when: PASS when root has no password (console disabled) or root MFA is enabled.
aws.a.iam.root_console_summary_mfa.fail_when: FAIL when root has a password and AccountMFAEnabled is 0.

aws.a.iam.root_hardware_mfa.description: Account-scope check that FAILs when AccountMFAEnabled is not 1, or when the virtual MFA device inventory has a device assigned to arn:aws:iam::<account>:root. Root protected only by a virtual (phone app) MFA is more exposed to device compromise or SIM/backup cloning than a hardware token, for the most powerful identity in the account.
aws.a.iam.root_hardware_mfa.pass_when: PASS when root MFA is enabled and no virtual MFA device is assigned to the root user.
aws.a.iam.root_hardware_mfa.fail_when: FAIL when root MFA is not enabled, or a virtual MFA device is assigned to root.

aws.a.iam.root_summary_mfa.description: Using the IAM account summary, FAILs when AccountMFAEnabled is 0, regardless of whether root has a console password. Root without MFA means a single leaked credential grants unrestricted, unblockable control of the whole account.

aws.a.iam.root_summary_no_keys.description: Using the IAM account summary, FAILs when AccountAccessKeysPresent is greater than zero, i.e. the root user has access keys. Root access keys are long-lived, cannot be limited by IAM policies or SCPs, and their leak gives full programmatic control of the account.
aws.a.iam.root_summary_no_keys.fail_when: FAIL when accountAccessKeysPresent is 1 or more.

aws.a.iam.server_certificate_expiry_date.description: For each IAM server certificate, FAILs when Expiration is earlier than 23:59:59 UTC of the day before the capture date, i.e. the certificate has already expired. Expired certificates left in IAM may still be attached to load balancers or CloudFront, causing TLS errors, or encouraging clients to bypass certificate validation.
aws.a.iam.server_certificate_expiry_date.pass_when: PASS when expiration is not before the previous-day 23:59:59 UTC cutoff.
aws.a.iam.server_certificate_expiry_date.fail_when: FAIL when expiration is before that cutoff (certificate expired).

aws.a.iam.unused_credentials_45_days.description: For each non-root credential-report user, FAILs when an enabled password or active access key was last used before 00:00 UTC of the capture date minus 45 days, or was never used and was created/rotated before that cutoff. Enabled but unused credentials are attack surface with no business value, and their abuse often goes unnoticed.
aws.a.iam.unused_credentials_45_days.pass_when: PASS when Every enabled password and active key was used, or created when never used, within the last 45 days.
aws.a.iam.unused_credentials_45_days.fail_when: FAIL when at least one enabled password or active key is stale beyond the 45-day cutoff.

aws.a.iam.unused_credentials_90_days.description: Same credential-report staleness logic with a 90-day window: for each non-root user, FAILs when an enabled password or active key's last use, or its creation/rotation if never used, is before 00:00 UTC of the capture date minus 90 days. Dormant credentials of departed staff or forgotten automation stay valid and can be used by an attacker.
aws.a.iam.unused_credentials_90_days.pass_when: PASS when Every enabled credential shows use or creation within the last 90 days.
aws.a.iam.unused_credentials_90_days.fail_when: FAIL when at least one enabled password or active key is stale beyond the 90-day cutoff.

aws.a.iam.user_no_cloudshell_full_access.description: For each IAM user, FAILs when AWSCloudShellFullAccess is directly attached to the user. The user can then open CloudShell sessions with their permissions and move files in or out, bypassing endpoint controls on data transfer.
aws.a.iam.user_no_cloudshell_full_access.pass_when: PASS when the user has no direct AWSCloudShellFullAccess attachment.
aws.a.iam.user_no_cloudshell_full_access.fail_when: FAIL when AWSCloudShellFullAccess is attached directly to the user.

aws.a.iam.user_no_direct_policies.description: For each IAM user, FAILs when the user has any directly attached managed policy or any inline (embedded) user policy. Permissions granted directly to users rather than through groups or roles are hard to review and revoke consistently, and they lead to privilege creep.
aws.a.iam.user_no_direct_policies.pass_when: PASS when the user has no attached managed policies and no inline policies.
aws.a.iam.user_no_direct_policies.fail_when: FAIL when the user has at least one attached managed policy or inline policy.

aws.a.iam.user_no_managed_policies.description: For each IAM user, FAILs when one or more managed policies (AWS or customer managed) are attached directly to the user; inline policies are not considered. Direct managed attachments bypass group-based access management and are easy to miss when access is reviewed.
aws.a.iam.user_no_managed_policies.pass_when: PASS when the user has no directly attached managed policies.
aws.a.iam.user_no_managed_policies.fail_when: FAIL when the user has at least one directly attached managed policy.

aws.a.kms.rotation_source_eligibility.description: For customer-managed symmetric (SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT) KMS keys that are not imported and not disabled or pending deletion, FAILs when KeyRotationEnabled is false. Without automatic rotation, the same key material protects data indefinitely, which increases the impact of any key-material exposure and fails cryptoperiod requirements.
aws.a.kms.rotation_source_eligibility.pass_when: PASS when the eligible key has KeyRotationEnabled true.
aws.a.kms.rotation_source_eligibility.fail_when: FAIL when the eligible key has KeyRotationEnabled false.
aws.a.kms.rotation_source_eligibility.not_applicable_when: Key is AWS-managed, has EXTERNAL (imported) origin, a non-SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT spec, or is Disabled/PendingDeletion.

aws.a.s3.bucket_account_public_blocks.description: For each S3 bucket, combines the bucket-level and account-level Public Access Block settings (each flag true at either level) and FAILs unless all four (BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, RestrictPublicBuckets) are effectively enabled. Any missing flag allows a public ACL or bucket policy to expose the bucket's data to the internet.
aws.a.s3.bucket_account_public_blocks.pass_when: PASS when All four flags are true at bucket level or, for each flag, at the account level.
aws.a.s3.bucket_account_public_blocks.fail_when: FAIL when at least one of the four flags is false at both bucket and account level (absent configs count as false).

aws.a.s3.default_encryption_configuratio.description: This S3 bucket check fails only when the native Encryption fact explicitly reports no default encryption configuration. A nonempty rules list with string SSEAlgorithm values passes, without requiring KMS or validating the algorithm choice.
aws.a.s3.default_encryption_configuratio.pass_when: PASS when at least one default encryption rule with an SSEAlgorithm is configured.
aws.a.s3.default_encryption_configuratio.fail_when: FAIL when the bucket encryption configuration is proven absent.

aws.a.s3.mfa_delete_enabled.description: For each S3 bucket, FAILs when its versioning configuration reports MFADelete Disabled or does not report MFADelete at all. Without MFA Delete, a compromised principal with s3:DeleteObjectVersion or s3:PutBucketVersioning can permanently destroy object versions, as in ransomware or evidence wiping.
aws.a.s3.mfa_delete_enabled.pass_when: PASS when versioning reports MFADelete Enabled.
aws.a.s3.mfa_delete_enabled.fail_when: FAIL when MFADelete is Disabled or not reported in collected versioning configuration.

aws.b.acm.expiry_thirty_days.description: For ACM certificates whose RenewalEligibility is ELIGIBLE, FAILs when the number of calendar days between the snapshot date and NotAfter is below 30. A certificate in use that is close to expiry and is not renewing (for example, DNS validation records were removed) will cause TLS outages and browser trust errors for the services fronted by it.
aws.b.acm.expiry_thirty_days.pass_when: PASS when notAfter is 30 or more calendar days after the snapshot date.
aws.b.acm.expiry_thirty_days.fail_when: FAIL when notAfter is fewer than 30 calendar days after the snapshot date (including already expired).
aws.b.acm.expiry_thirty_days.not_applicable_when: RenewalEligibility is INELIGIBLE (certificate not associated with an AWS service).

aws.b.acm.no_failed_validation.description: For each ACM certificate, FAILs when Status is FAILED or VALIDATION_TIMED_OUT. Such certificates were never issued; leftover failed requests clutter inventory and can indicate a broken domain validation that leaves intended endpoints without valid TLS.
aws.b.acm.no_failed_validation.pass_when: PASS when status is ISSUED, PENDING_VALIDATION, INACTIVE, EXPIRED or REVOKED.
aws.b.acm.no_failed_validation.fail_when: FAIL when status is FAILED or VALIDATION_TIMED_OUT.

aws.b.acm.no_wildcard_domain.description: For each ACM certificate, FAILs when the primary DomainName starts with '*' (wildcard certificate). The private key of a wildcard certificate can impersonate every subdomain, so one compromised host or misused key exposes all sibling services; only the primary name is checked, not SANs.
aws.b.acm.no_wildcard_domain.pass_when: PASS when the primary DomainName does not start with '*'.
aws.b.acm.no_wildcard_domain.fail_when: FAIL when the primary DomainName starts with '*'.

aws.b.acm.not_past_expiry_date.description: For renewal-eligible ACM certificates, FAILs when the calendar date of NotAfter is before the snapshot date, i.e. the in-use certificate has already expired. Expired certificates on load balancers, CloudFront or API Gateway break TLS for clients and push users to ignore certificate warnings.
aws.b.acm.not_past_expiry_date.pass_when: PASS when notAfter's date is on or after the snapshot date.
aws.b.acm.not_past_expiry_date.fail_when: FAIL when notAfter's date is before the snapshot date.

aws.b.acm.pending_validation_review.description: For each ACM certificate, returns MANUAL when Status is PENDING_VALIDATION so the owner can confirm whether the outstanding domain validation is expected; every other recognised status PASSes. Long-pending requests usually mean DNS/email validation was never completed and the intended endpoint lacks its certificate.
aws.b.acm.pending_validation_review.pass_when: PASS when status is anything other than PENDING_VALIDATION (ISSUED, EXPIRED, FAILED, etc.).
aws.b.acm.pending_validation_review.fail_when: FAIL when never returns FAIL; PENDING_VALIDATION is reported as MANUAL for review.

aws.b.acm.rsa_minimum_2048.description: For RSA ACM certificates, FAILs when KeyAlgorithm is RSA_1024 (or RSA-1024), i.e. the key is under 2048 bits. 1024-bit RSA keys are considered breakable by well-resourced attackers and are rejected by modern clients, which undermines the TLS session confidentiality.
aws.b.acm.rsa_minimum_2048.pass_when: PASS when keyAlgorithm is RSA_2048, RSA_3072 or RSA_4096.
aws.b.acm.rsa_minimum_2048.not_applicable_when: KeyAlgorithm is an elliptic-curve algorithm (EC_prime256v1, EC_secp384r1, EC_secp521r1).

aws.b.acm.transparency_logging.description: For AMAZON_ISSUED and PRIVATE ACM certificates, FAILs when Options.CertificateTransparencyLoggingPreference is DISABLED. Without CT logging, publicly trusted certificates are rejected by browsers like Chrome, and domain owners lose the public log needed to spot mis-issued certificates for their domains.

aws.b.alb.access_logs.description: For Application Load Balancers, FAILs when the load balancer attribute access_logs.s3.enabled is not 'true'. Without ALB access logs, there is no per-request record (client IP, path, TLS cipher, response code) to investigate attacks, scanning or data exfiltration through the load balancer.
aws.b.alb.access_logs.not_applicable_when: Load balancer Type is network or gateway.

aws.b.alb.deletion_protection.description: For Application Load Balancers, FAILs when the attribute deletion_protection.enabled is not 'true'. Without deletion protection, an accidental or malicious DeleteLoadBalancer call immediately takes the application offline.
aws.b.alb.deletion_protection.not_applicable_when: Load balancer Type is network or gateway.

aws.b.alb.desync_mode.description: For Application Load Balancers, FAILs when routing.http.desync_mitigation_mode is 'monitor'. In monitor mode the ALB forwards ambiguous requests, which allows HTTP request smuggling/desync attacks against backend targets; defensive and strictest modes pass.
aws.b.alb.desync_mode.pass_when: PASS when desync mitigation mode is defensive or strictest.
aws.b.alb.desync_mode.fail_when: FAIL when desync mitigation mode is monitor.
aws.b.alb.desync_mode.not_applicable_when: Load balancer Type is not application.

aws.b.alb.invalid_header_dropping.description: For Application Load Balancers, FAILs when routing.http.drop_invalid_header_fields.enabled is not 'true'. If invalid HTTP header names are forwarded, malformed headers can reach the backend and be used for header-injection or request-smuggling style attacks.
aws.b.alb.invalid_header_dropping.not_applicable_when: Load balancer Type is network or gateway.

aws.b.apigateway.client_certificate.description: For each REST API stage, FAILs when no clientCertificateId is set on the stage. Without a client certificate, backend HTTP integrations cannot verify that requests really come from API Gateway, so anyone who finds the backend URL can call it directly and skip API Gateway authorization.
aws.b.apigateway.client_certificate.pass_when: PASS when the stage declares a clientCertificateId.
aws.b.apigateway.client_certificate.fail_when: FAIL when the stage has no clientCertificateId.

aws.b.apigateway.http_execution_logging.description: For HTTP API (API Gateway v2) stages, FAILs when DefaultRouteSettings.LoggingLevel is OFF, empty or not set. Without execution logging, failed authorizations, integration errors and abusive calls through the API cannot be traced.
aws.b.apigateway.http_execution_logging.pass_when: PASS when loggingLevel is INFO or ERROR.
aws.b.apigateway.http_execution_logging.fail_when: FAIL when loggingLevel is OFF, empty or absent.

aws.b.apigateway.private_endpoint_type.description: For each REST API, FAILs when endpointConfiguration.types does not include PRIVATE (i.e. it is REGIONAL or EDGE only). Non-private APIs are reachable from the internet, so authorization and throttling are the only barrier to scanning and attacks.
aws.b.apigateway.private_endpoint_type.pass_when: PASS when the endpoint types include PRIVATE.
aws.b.apigateway.private_endpoint_type.fail_when: FAIL when the endpoint types contain only REGIONAL and/or EDGE.

aws.b.apigateway.rest_execution_logging.description: For REST API stages, FAILs when the wildcard '*/*' method setting has loggingLevel OFF, empty or unset. Without CloudWatch execution logs, request processing errors, authorizer denials and attack traffic against the API leave no trace.
aws.b.apigateway.rest_execution_logging.pass_when: PASS when the '*/*' method setting loggingLevel is INFO or ERROR.
aws.b.apigateway.rest_execution_logging.fail_when: FAIL when loggingLevel is OFF, empty or not configured.

aws.b.apigateway.rest_xray.description: For REST API stages, FAILs when tracingEnabled is false. Without X-Ray tracing, latency and error paths across API Gateway and backends cannot be followed, which makes abuse and failure analysis harder.

aws.b.apigateway.waf_reference.description: For REST API stages, FAILs when the stage has no webAclArn association. Without AWS WAF in front of the stage, common web exploits (SQLi, XSS, bad bots, volumetric abuse) reach the API and its integrations unfiltered.
aws.b.apigateway.waf_reference.pass_when: PASS when the stage declares a webAclArn.
aws.b.apigateway.waf_reference.fail_when: FAIL when the stage has no webAclArn.

aws.b.apigateway.wildcard_cache_encrypti.description: For REST API stages, FAILs unless the wildcard '*/*' method setting has both cachingEnabled and cacheDataEncrypted set to true. Stages that do not enable caching also FAIL. When caching is enabled without encryption, cached responses that may contain sensitive data are stored unencrypted at rest.
aws.b.apigateway.wildcard_cache_encrypti.pass_when: PASS when both cachingEnabled and cacheDataEncrypted are true in the '*/*' settings.
aws.b.apigateway.wildcard_cache_encrypti.fail_when: FAIL when either cachingEnabled or cacheDataEncrypted is false or missing.

aws.b.aurora.mysql_audit_export.description: For RDS clusters with Engine exactly aurora-mysql, FAILs when EnabledCloudwatchLogsExports does not contain 'audit'. Without exported audit logs, database logins, privilege changes and queries against sensitive tables are not kept off-host for detection or forensics.
aws.b.aurora.mysql_audit_export.pass_when: PASS when 'audit' is in the exported log types.
aws.b.aurora.mysql_audit_export.fail_when: FAIL when 'audit' is not exported to CloudWatch Logs.

aws.b.aurora.mysql_copy_snapshot_tags.description: For RDS clusters with Engine aurora-mysql, FAILs when CopyTagsToSnapshot is false. Snapshots without the cluster's tags lose ownership, classification and tag-based access-control (ABAC) metadata, so sensitive backups can be mishandled or escape tag-scoped policies.

aws.b.aurora.postgres_copy_snapshot_tags.description: For RDS clusters with Engine aurora-postgresql, FAILs when CopyTagsToSnapshot is false. Untagged snapshots of PostgreSQL-compatible Aurora clusters lose data-classification and ownership tags, which breaks tag-based retention, cost and access policies for backup copies.

aws.b.backup.report_plan_presence.description: Scope-level check per region that FAILs when at least one AWS Backup plan exists but the completely collected backup report plan inventory is empty. Without report plans, nobody gets audit reports on backup job success or compliance, so failed or missing backups go unnoticed.
aws.b.backup.report_plan_presence.pass_when: PASS when backup plans exist and at least one backup report plan exists.
aws.b.backup.report_plan_presence.fail_when: FAIL when backup plans exist and no backup report plan exists.

aws.b.backup_plan.regional_presence.description: Scope-level check per account/region that FAILs when the completely collected AWS Backup plan inventory is empty. A region with no backup plan has no policy-driven, scheduled backups, so resources there may not be recoverable after deletion, ransomware or corruption.
aws.b.backup_plan.regional_presence.pass_when: PASS when at least one backup plan exists in the region.
aws.b.backup_plan.regional_presence.fail_when: FAIL when the region's backup plan inventory is complete and empty.

aws.b.backup_vault.regional_presence.description: Scope-level check per account/region that FAILs when the completely collected AWS Backup vault inventory is empty. Without a vault, there is no encrypted, access-controlled place to store recovery points in that region.
aws.b.backup_vault.regional_presence.pass_when: PASS when at least one backup vault exists in the region.
aws.b.backup_vault.regional_presence.fail_when: FAIL when the region's backup vault inventory is complete and empty.

aws.b.classic_elb.access_logs.description: For Classic Load Balancers, FAILs when LoadBalancerAttributes.AccessLog.Enabled is false. Without access logs, requests that pass through the legacy ELB (source IPs, URLs, backend responses) cannot be reconstructed during incident response.

aws.b.classic_elb.connection_draining.description: For Classic Load Balancers, FAILs when ConnectionDraining.Enabled is false. Without connection draining, in-flight requests are cut off when an instance is deregistered or becomes unhealthy, causing user-visible errors and possible partial transactions.

aws.b.classic_elb.cross_zone.description: For Classic Load Balancers, FAILs when CrossZoneLoadBalancing.Enabled is false. Traffic is then split per AZ rather than per instance, so an AZ with fewer healthy instances can be overloaded, which reduces resilience during partial outages.

aws.b.classic_elb.desync_mode.description: For Classic Load Balancers, FAILs when the additional attribute elb.http.desyncmitigationmode is 'monitor'. Monitor mode passes ambiguous HTTP requests to instances, which leaves backends open to HTTP request smuggling.
aws.b.classic_elb.desync_mode.pass_when: PASS when the desync mode is defensive or strictest.
aws.b.classic_elb.desync_mode.fail_when: FAIL when the desync mode is monitor.

aws.b.classic_elb.encrypted_listeners.description: For Classic Load Balancers with listeners, FAILs when any listener's front-end Protocol is not HTTPS, SSL or TLS (for example HTTP or TCP). Plaintext listeners expose credentials, session cookies and data to interception between clients and the load balancer.
aws.b.classic_elb.encrypted_listeners.pass_when: PASS when Every listener uses HTTPS, SSL or TLS.
aws.b.classic_elb.encrypted_listeners.fail_when: FAIL when at least one listener uses HTTP, TCP or another non-TLS protocol.
aws.b.classic_elb.encrypted_listeners.not_applicable_when: The load balancer has no listener descriptions.

aws.b.classic_elb.multiple_az.description: For Classic Load Balancers, FAILs when the AvailabilityZones list has fewer than two entries. A single-AZ load balancer and its targets go down with that zone, so there is no fault tolerance.
aws.b.classic_elb.multiple_az.pass_when: PASS when two or more availability zones are declared.
aws.b.classic_elb.multiple_az.fail_when: FAIL when fewer than two availability zones are declared.

aws.b.cloudfront.access_logging.description: For CloudFront distributions, FAILs when DistributionConfig.Logging.Enabled is false (standard access logging off). Without edge access logs, requests, viewer IPs and abuse patterns against the CDN cannot be investigated.

aws.b.cloudfront.custom_acm_certificate.description: For CloudFront distributions, FAILs unless the ViewerCertificate declares both ACMCertificateArn and Certificate. Distributions on the default *.cloudfront.net certificate, and distributions with an IAM-uploaded certificate, FAIL. Without a custom ACM certificate the service is not served on its own validated domain with a centrally renewed key.
aws.b.cloudfront.custom_acm_certificate.pass_when: PASS when both ACMCertificateArn and Certificate are present.
aws.b.cloudfront.custom_acm_certificate.fail_when: FAIL when either reference is missing (for example CloudFrontDefaultCertificate or an IAM certificate).

aws.b.cloudfront.custom_origin_encryptio.description: For CloudFront distributions, FAILs when any custom origin uses OriginProtocolPolicy http-only, or uses match-viewer while any cache behavior allows HTTP viewers (allow-all). In both cases content and headers travel in cleartext between CloudFront and the origin, where they can be intercepted or altered.
aws.b.cloudfront.custom_origin_encryptio.pass_when: PASS when Every custom origin is https-only, or match-viewer with no allow-all behavior.
aws.b.cloudfront.custom_origin_encryptio.fail_when: FAIL when a custom origin is http-only, or match-viewer while some behavior permits HTTP viewers.

aws.b.cloudfront.default_root_object.description: For CloudFront distributions, FAILs when DefaultRootObject is an empty string. Without a default root object, a request to the distribution root is forwarded to the origin as-is, which can expose an S3 bucket listing or the origin's default page.
aws.b.cloudfront.default_root_object.pass_when: PASS when defaultRootObject is a non-empty value.

aws.b.cloudfront.field_level_encryption.description: For CloudFront distributions, FAILs when DefaultCacheBehavior.FieldLevelEncryptionId is empty. Without field-level encryption, sensitive form fields (cards, PII) submitted through the default behavior are visible in clear text to every downstream system after TLS ends at the edge.
aws.b.cloudfront.field_level_encryption.pass_when: PASS when the default behavior has a non-empty FieldLevelEncryptionId.
aws.b.cloudfront.field_level_encryption.fail_when: FAIL when fieldLevelEncryptionId is empty on the default behavior.

aws.b.cloudfront.geo_restrictions.description: For CloudFront distributions, FAILs when Restrictions.GeoRestriction.RestrictionType is 'none'. With no allow-list or block-list of countries, content is served globally, including to regions where the business has no users or where sanctions or licensing require blocking.
aws.b.cloudfront.geo_restrictions.pass_when: PASS when restrictionType is whitelist or blacklist.

aws.b.cloudfront.no_sslv3_origin.description: For CloudFront distributions, FAILs when any custom origin's OriginSslProtocols includes SSLv3. SSLv3 is vulnerable to POODLE, so CloudFront-to-origin traffic negotiated with it can be decrypted by a network attacker.
aws.b.cloudfront.no_sslv3_origin.pass_when: PASS when no custom origin lists SSLv3.
aws.b.cloudfront.no_sslv3_origin.fail_when: FAIL when at least one custom origin allows SSLv3.

aws.b.cloudfront.origin_group_metadata.description: For CloudFront distributions, FAILs when DistributionConfig.OriginGroups has no Items element. Without an origin group, there is no origin failover, so a failing primary origin directly causes outages at the edge.
aws.b.cloudfront.origin_group_metadata.pass_when: PASS when originGroups contains an Items list.
aws.b.cloudfront.origin_group_metadata.fail_when: FAIL when originGroups has no Items (no origin groups declared).

aws.b.cloudfront.origin_secure_protocols.description: For CloudFront distributions, FAILs when any custom origin's OriginSslProtocols includes SSLv3 or TLSv1 (1.0). These deprecated protocols have known weaknesses (POODLE, BEAST), so origin-leg encryption can be downgraded or broken.
aws.b.cloudfront.origin_secure_protocols.pass_when: PASS when no custom origin allows SSLv3 or TLSv1.
aws.b.cloudfront.origin_secure_protocols.fail_when: FAIL when at least one custom origin allows SSLv3 or TLSv1.

aws.b.cloudfront.sni.description: For CloudFront distributions, FAILs when ViewerCertificate.SSLSupportMethod is 'vip' or 'static-ip' instead of 'sni-only'. Dedicated-IP TLS serving costs about USD 600/month per distribution and is only needed for very old clients without SNI support.
aws.b.cloudfront.sni.fail_when: FAIL when sSLSupportMethod is vip or static-ip.

aws.b.cloudfront.viewer_encryption.description: For CloudFront distributions, FAILs when the default cache behavior or any additional cache behavior has ViewerProtocolPolicy 'allow-all'. Behaviors that accept HTTP let viewers' requests, cookies and responses travel unencrypted and be intercepted or modified.
aws.b.cloudfront.viewer_encryption.pass_when: PASS when All behaviors use https-only or redirect-to-https.
aws.b.cloudfront.viewer_encryption.fail_when: FAIL when at least one behavior uses allow-all.

aws.b.cloudfront.waf_reference.description: For CloudFront distributions, FAILs when DistributionConfig.WebACLId is empty. Without a WAF web ACL, the edge cannot filter common exploits, bad bots or layer-7 floods before they reach the origin.

aws.b.codebuild.artifact_encryption.description: For CodeBuild projects, FAILs unless the primary artifact explicitly declares encryptionDisabled=false, or when any secondary artifact declares encryptionDisabled=true. This literal source rule also FAILs projects whose primary artifact omits the flag. The aim is to stop build outputs, which can include binaries, configs and secrets, from being stored without encryption.
aws.b.codebuild.artifact_encryption.pass_when: PASS when primary artifact declares encryptionDisabled false and no secondary artifact declares it true.
aws.b.codebuild.artifact_encryption.fail_when: FAIL when primary artifact's encryptionDisabled is true or omitted, or any secondary artifact has encryptionDisabled true.

aws.b.codebuild.logs_enabled.description: For CodeBuild projects, FAILs when neither logsConfig.cloudWatchLogs.status nor logsConfig.s3Logs.status is ENABLED (missing blocks count as disabled). Without build logs, malicious buildspec changes, dependency-confusion pulls or leaked secrets in builds cannot be audited.
aws.b.codebuild.logs_enabled.pass_when: PASS when cloudWatch Logs or S3 logs is ENABLED.
aws.b.codebuild.logs_enabled.fail_when: FAIL when both CloudWatch and S3 log destinations are DISABLED or absent.

aws.b.codebuild.nonprivileged.description: For CodeBuild projects, FAILs when environment.privilegedMode is true. Privileged mode runs the build container with root access to the Docker daemon on the host, so a malicious or compromised build step can escape the container and tamper with the build environment.

aws.b.codebuild.s3_artifact_encryption.description: For CodeBuild projects with S3-type primary or secondary artifacts, FAILs when any S3 artifact sets encryptionDisabled=true; an omitted flag is treated as the default encrypted. Unencrypted artifacts in S3 can expose build outputs and embedded secrets to anyone with bucket read access.
aws.b.codebuild.s3_artifact_encryption.pass_when: PASS when no S3 artifact has encryptionDisabled true.
aws.b.codebuild.s3_artifact_encryption.fail_when: FAIL when at least one S3 artifact has encryptionDisabled true.
aws.b.codebuild.s3_artifact_encryption.not_applicable_when: The project has no S3 artifacts (only NO_ARTIFACTS or CODEPIPELINE).

aws.b.codebuild.s3_log_encryption.description: For CodeBuild projects, FAILs when logsConfig.s3Logs.encryptionDisabled is true. Build logs often contain environment details, URLs and sometimes secrets, and storing them unencrypted in S3 widens exposure.

aws.b.cognito.admin_only_signup.description: For Cognito user pools, FAILs when AdminCreateUserConfig.AllowAdminCreateUserOnly is false (an omitted value is treated as false), meaning self-service sign-up is open. Open self-registration lets anyone create an authenticated identity, which may be accepted by apps or identity pools that assume users were vetted.
aws.b.cognito.admin_only_signup.fail_when: FAIL when AllowAdminCreateUserOnly is false or omitted.

aws.b.cognito.block_all_takeover_risks.description: For Cognito user pools, FAILs unless threat protection (AdvancedSecurityMode) is ENFORCED and the account-takeover risk configuration sets EventAction BLOCK for the Low, Medium and High risk levels. Any weaker response (NO_ACTION, MFA_IF_CONFIGURED, MFA_REQUIRED) lets risky sign-ins proceed, which allows credential-stuffing takeovers.
aws.b.cognito.block_all_takeover_risks.pass_when: PASS when mode is ENFORCED and all three risk levels are BLOCK.
aws.b.cognito.block_all_takeover_risks.fail_when: FAIL when mode is not ENFORCED, or any risk level's action is not BLOCK.

aws.b.cognito.block_compromised_signin.description: For Cognito user pools, FAILs unless AdvancedSecurityMode is ENFORCED and CompromisedCredentialsRiskConfiguration includes SIGN_IN in its EventFilter with EventAction BLOCK. Otherwise users whose passwords appear in breach corpora can still sign in, which enables account takeover through leaked credentials.
aws.b.cognito.block_compromised_signin.pass_when: PASS when mode ENFORCED, EventFilter contains SIGN_IN and EventAction is BLOCK.
aws.b.cognito.block_compromised_signin.fail_when: FAIL when mode not ENFORCED, SIGN_IN not filtered, or action not BLOCK.

aws.b.cognito.deletion_protection.description: For Cognito user pools, FAILs when DeletionProtection is not ACTIVE (an omitted value is treated as INACTIVE). A user pool deleted by mistake or maliciously cannot be recovered, which destroys every user identity and locks all users out of dependent applications.
aws.b.cognito.deletion_protection.fail_when: FAIL when deletionProtection is INACTIVE or omitted.

aws.b.cognito.enforced_threat_protection.description: For Cognito user pools, FAILs when UserPoolAddOns.AdvancedSecurityMode is AUDIT or OFF (an omitted value is treated as OFF) instead of ENFORCED. In audit/off modes, risky or compromised-credential sign-ins are at most logged, never blocked or challenged.
aws.b.cognito.enforced_threat_protection.fail_when: FAIL when advancedSecurityMode is AUDIT, OFF or omitted.

aws.b.cognito.no_guest_identities.description: For Cognito identity pools, FAILs when AllowUnauthenticatedIdentities is true. Guest identities let anyone on the internet obtain temporary AWS credentials for the pool's unauthenticated IAM role, which is a common path to data exposure if that role is over-permissioned.

aws.b.cognito.password_lowercase.description: For Cognito user pools, FAILs when Policies.PasswordPolicy.RequireLowercase is false or not set, so end-user passwords need not contain lowercase letters. Weaker composition makes application-user accounts easier to brute-force or credential-stuff.
aws.b.cognito.password_lowercase.fail_when: FAIL when requireLowercase is false or omitted.

aws.b.cognito.password_minimum_fourteen.description: For Cognito user pools, FAILs when Policies.PasswordPolicy.MinimumLength is below 14 (an omitted value counts as 0). Short minimum lengths for application users make online guessing and offline cracking of passwords much easier.
aws.b.cognito.password_minimum_fourteen.pass_when: PASS when minimumLength is 14 or more.
aws.b.cognito.password_minimum_fourteen.fail_when: FAIL when minimumLength is below 14 or omitted.

aws.b.cognito.password_number.description: For Cognito user pools, FAILs when Policies.PasswordPolicy.RequireNumbers is false or not set, so end-user passwords need not contain digits. Weaker composition makes application-user accounts easier to brute-force or credential-stuff.
aws.b.cognito.password_number.fail_when: FAIL when requireNumbers is false or omitted.

aws.b.cognito.password_policy.description: For Cognito user pools, composite check that FAILs when MinimumLength is below 8, TemporaryPasswordValidityDays is above 7, or any of RequireLowercase, RequireUppercase, RequireNumbers or RequireSymbols is false or missing. This baseline protects pool users from trivially weak passwords and long-lived temporary passwords.
aws.b.cognito.password_policy.pass_when: PASS when length is 8 or more, temporary validity is 7 days or less, and all four character classes are required.
aws.b.cognito.password_policy.fail_when: FAIL when any of the length, temporary-validity or character-class conditions is not met.

aws.b.cognito.password_symbol.description: For Cognito user pools, FAILs when Policies.PasswordPolicy.RequireSymbols is false or not set, so end-user passwords need not contain special characters. Weaker composition makes application-user accounts easier to brute-force or credential-stuff.
aws.b.cognito.password_symbol.fail_when: FAIL when requireSymbols is false or omitted.

aws.b.cognito.password_uppercase.description: For Cognito user pools, FAILs when Policies.PasswordPolicy.RequireUppercase is false or not set, so end-user passwords need not contain uppercase letters. Weaker composition makes application-user accounts easier to brute-force or credential-stuff.
aws.b.cognito.password_uppercase.fail_when: FAIL when requireUppercase is false or omitted.

aws.b.cognito.required_mfa.description: For Cognito user pools, FAILs when MfaConfiguration is OFF or OPTIONAL rather than ON. With MFA optional or off, most users sign in with a password alone, so phished or stuffed credentials give direct account access.
aws.b.cognito.required_mfa.fail_when: FAIL when mfaConfiguration is OFF, OPTIONAL or omitted.

aws.b.cognito.temporary_password_seven_d.description: For Cognito user pools, FAILs when Policies.PasswordPolicy.TemporaryPasswordValidityDays is greater than 7 (0/omitted is treated as the 7-day default). Admin-issued temporary passwords that stay valid for a long time can be intercepted from invitation emails and used before the real user signs in.
aws.b.cognito.temporary_password_seven_d.pass_when: PASS when temporaryPasswordValidityDays is 7 or less (or unset).
aws.b.cognito.temporary_password_seven_d.fail_when: FAIL when temporaryPasswordValidityDays is greater than 7.

aws.b.dms.automatic_minor_upgrade.description: For DMS replication instances, FAILs when AutoMinorVersionUpgrade is false. The replication engine then keeps running versions that are missing security and bug fixes until someone upgrades it by hand.

aws.b.dms.multi_az.description: For DMS replication instances, FAILs when MultiAZ is false. A single-AZ replication instance stops ongoing migration/CDC tasks during an AZ or host failure, which risks data lag or replication gaps.

aws.b.dms.no_public_instance.description: For DMS replication instances, FAILs when PubliclyAccessible is true. A public replication instance has a public IP from which source/target database credentials and replicated data paths can be reached or attacked from the internet.

aws.b.docdb.deletion_protection.description: For DocumentDB clusters, FAILs when DeletionProtection is false. Without it, one DeleteDBCluster call, whether accidental or made by an attacker, destroys the cluster and its data.

aws.b.docdb.seven_day_backups.description: For DocumentDB clusters, FAILs when BackupRetentionPeriod is less than 7 days. Short automatic backup retention limits point-in-time recovery after corruption or ransomware discovered more than a few days later.
aws.b.docdb.seven_day_backups.pass_when: PASS when backupRetentionPeriod is 7 or more.

aws.b.docdb.storage_encryption.description: For DocumentDB clusters, FAILs when StorageEncrypted is false. Unencrypted storage, snapshots and replicas expose document data if underlying volumes or snapshot copies are accessed outside the database.

aws.b.dynamodb.deletion_protection.description: For DynamoDB tables, FAILs when Table.DeletionProtectionEnabled is false. An unprotected table can be dropped with a single DeleteTable call, which loses production data immediately.

aws.b.dynamodb.encryption_type.description: For DynamoDB tables, FAILs only when an SSEDescription is present with SSEType AES256. Tables with no SSEDescription (AWS-owned default key) or with SSEType KMS pass. This separates the documented default and KMS-backed encryption from the legacy AES256 SSE type.
aws.b.dynamodb.encryption_type.pass_when: PASS when no SSEDescription (default owned-key encryption) or SSEType KMS.

aws.b.dynamodb.kms_description.description: Checks only whether a DynamoDB table has an SSEDescription object. AES256 can pass; the check does not verify SSEType=KMS, KMS key identity, or effective KMS encryption.
aws.b.dynamodb.kms_description.pass_when: PASS when table.Table.SSEDescription is a dictionary, regardless of SSEType or key reference.

aws.b.dynamodb.point_in_time_recovery.description: For DynamoDB tables, FAILs when PointInTimeRecoveryStatus is DISABLED. Without PITR, accidental writes, deletes or malicious overwrites can only be recovered from on-demand backups, if any exist, rather than to any second in the last 35 days.

aws.b.ecr.all_tags_immutable.description: For ECR repositories, FAILs when imageTagMutability is anything other than IMMUTABLE, including MUTABLE and both *_WITH_EXCLUSION modes. Mutable tags let a pusher silently replace the image behind an existing tag such as 'prod' or 'v1.2', which enables supply-chain substitution of deployed images.
aws.b.ecr.all_tags_immutable.fail_when: FAIL when imageTagMutability is MUTABLE, MUTABLE_WITH_EXCLUSION or IMMUTABLE_WITH_EXCLUSION.

aws.b.ecr.effective_scan_configuration.description: For ECR repositories, resolves the registry scanning configuration: under BASIC scanning it FAILs when the repository's scanOnPush is false; under ENHANCED scanning it FAILs when no SCAN_ON_PUSH or CONTINUOUS_SCAN rule's wildcard filter matches the repository name. Unscanned repositories let images with known CVEs reach deployment unnoticed.
aws.b.ecr.effective_scan_configuration.pass_when: PASS when bASIC with scanOnPush true, or ENHANCED with a matching on-push/continuous rule.
aws.b.ecr.effective_scan_configuration.fail_when: FAIL when bASIC with scanOnPush false, or ENHANCED with no matching on-push/continuous rule.

aws.b.ecr.lifecycle_rules.description: For ECR repositories, FAILs when no lifecycle policy exists or the policy JSON has no 'rules' key. Without lifecycle rules, old and vulnerable images pile up indefinitely, which increases cost and the chance that a stale vulnerable image gets deployed.
aws.b.ecr.lifecycle_rules.pass_when: PASS when a lifecycle policy with a rules array exists.
aws.b.ecr.lifecycle_rules.fail_when: FAIL when the lifecycle policy is absent or lacks rules.

aws.b.ecr.source_some_immutability.description: For ECR repositories, FAILs only when imageTagMutability is exactly MUTABLE. Any IMMUTABLE or *_WITH_EXCLUSION mode passes. This is the weaker Prowler criterion: it catches repositories where every tag can be overwritten, which allows image substitution attacks.
aws.b.ecr.source_some_immutability.pass_when: PASS when imageTagMutability is IMMUTABLE, IMMUTABLE_WITH_EXCLUSION or MUTABLE_WITH_EXCLUSION.

aws.b.ecs.all_readonly_roots.description: For ECS task definitions, FAILs when any container definition does not set readonlyRootFilesystem true (an omitted value counts as writable). A writable root filesystem lets an attacker who compromises the container drop binaries, modify configs or persist tooling.
aws.b.ecs.all_readonly_roots.pass_when: PASS when Every container declares readonlyRootFilesystem true.
aws.b.ecs.all_readonly_roots.fail_when: FAIL when at least one container has a writable root filesystem.

aws.b.ecs.declared_nonroot_users.description: For ECS task definitions, FAILs when any container's 'user' is root or UID 0. If no container is root but some do not declare a user (inheriting the image default), the result is UNKNOWN. Containers running as root give a compromised process full in-container privilege and an easier path to host escape.
aws.b.ecs.declared_nonroot_users.pass_when: PASS when Every container explicitly declares a non-root user/UID.
aws.b.ecs.declared_nonroot_users.fail_when: FAIL when any container declares user root or UID 0.

aws.b.ecs.host_network_nonprivileged.description: For ECS task definitions with networkMode 'host', FAILs when any container is privileged or runs as root/UID 0; undeclared users give UNKNOWN. Host networking already shares the instance's network stack, and adding privilege or root lets a container compromise reach the host and its other tasks.
aws.b.ecs.host_network_nonprivileged.pass_when: PASS when host-mode task has no privileged containers and every container declares a non-root user.
aws.b.ecs.host_network_nonprivileged.fail_when: FAIL when host-mode task has a privileged container or a root/UID 0 container.
aws.b.ecs.host_network_nonprivileged.not_applicable_when: networkMode is none, bridge or awsvpc.

aws.b.ecs.no_host_pid.description: For ECS task definitions, FAILs when pidMode is 'host'. Sharing the host PID namespace lets containers see and signal every process on the instance, which exposes other tasks' secrets through /proc and enables process injection.
aws.b.ecs.no_host_pid.pass_when: PASS when pidMode is 'task' or not set.

aws.b.ecs.no_privileged_containers.description: For ECS task definitions, FAILs when any container definition sets privileged true. Privileged containers get nearly all host kernel capabilities and device access, so a compromise of the container amounts to a compromise of the EC2 container instance.
aws.b.ecs.no_privileged_containers.pass_when: PASS when no container has privileged true.
aws.b.ecs.no_privileged_containers.fail_when: FAIL when at least one container has privileged true.

aws.b.ecs.some_logging_configuration.description: For ECS task definitions, FAILs when no container defines a logConfiguration. This is an existential test, so one logged container makes the task pass. Tasks with no log driver produce no stdout/stderr records for detecting or investigating malicious activity.
aws.b.ecs.some_logging_configuration.pass_when: PASS when at least one container declares a logConfiguration.
aws.b.ecs.some_logging_configuration.fail_when: FAIL when no container declares a logConfiguration.

aws.b.efs.at_rest_encryption.description: For EFS file systems, FAILs when Encrypted is false. Unencrypted EFS data and backups are not protected by KMS, so access to the underlying storage or backup copies exposes file contents.

aws.b.efs.customer_managed_key.description: For EFS file systems, FAILs when the file system is unencrypted, or when its KmsKeyId resolves in the KMS inventory to an AWS-managed key or to a customer key that is disabled. Using an enabled customer-managed key gives the owner key-policy control, auditing and the ability to revoke access to the data.
aws.b.efs.customer_managed_key.pass_when: PASS when encrypted with a KMS key whose KeyManager is CUSTOMER and Enabled is true.
aws.b.efs.customer_managed_key.fail_when: FAIL when not encrypted, or the key is AWS-managed or disabled.

aws.b.eks.audit_log_category.description: For EKS clusters, FAILs when no clusterLogging entry is enabled with the 'audit' log type. Without Kubernetes API audit logs in CloudWatch, nothing records who read secrets, created privileged pods or changed RBAC.
aws.b.eks.audit_log_category.pass_when: PASS when an enabled clusterLogging entry includes 'audit'.
aws.b.eks.audit_log_category.fail_when: FAIL when no enabled entry includes 'audit'.

aws.b.eks.disable_public_endpoint.description: For EKS clusters, FAILs when resourcesVpcConfig.endpointPublicAccess is true and publicAccessCidrs contains 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 (or is unset, which defaults to 0.0.0.0/0). An internet-wide Kubernetes API endpoint is exposed to credential brute-force and exploitation of API server vulnerabilities.
aws.b.eks.disable_public_endpoint.pass_when: PASS when public access is disabled, or restricted to specific non-wildcard CIDRs.
aws.b.eks.disable_public_endpoint.fail_when: FAIL when public access is enabled for 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0.

aws.b.eks.no_default_vpc.description: For EKS clusters, joins resourcesVpcConfig.vpcId to the VPC inventory and FAILs when that VPC has IsDefault true. The default VPC has public subnets and permissive defaults that were not designed for workload isolation, so nodes and pods may be internet-reachable.
aws.b.eks.no_default_vpc.pass_when: PASS when the cluster's VPC is not a default VPC.
aws.b.eks.no_default_vpc.fail_when: FAIL when the cluster runs in the account's default VPC.

aws.b.eks.secret_envelope_encryption.description: For EKS clusters running Kubernetes below 1.28, FAILs when no encryptionConfig entry lists 'secrets' as a resource. Clusters on 1.28 or later pass because of EKS default envelope encryption. Without KMS envelope encryption, Kubernetes Secrets in etcd are protected only by the volume encryption.
aws.b.eks.secret_envelope_encryption.pass_when: PASS when version is 1.28 or later, or an encryptionConfig includes 'secrets'.
aws.b.eks.secret_envelope_encryption.fail_when: FAIL when version is below 1.28 and no encryptionConfig covers 'secrets'.

aws.b.elasticache.at_rest.description: For ElastiCache replication groups, FAILs when AtRestEncryptionEnabled is false. Cached data, backups and swap on disk are then unencrypted, which exposes session tokens or PII held in Redis/Valkey.

aws.b.elasticache.automatic_failover.description: For ElastiCache replication groups, FAILs when AutomaticFailover is not 'enabled' (disabled, enabling, disabling). Without automatic failover, a primary node failure leaves the cache read-only or unavailable until someone intervenes.
aws.b.elasticache.automatic_failover.fail_when: FAIL when automaticFailover is disabled, enabling or disabling.

aws.b.elasticache.automatic_minor_upgrad.description: For ElastiCache cache clusters, FAILs when AutoMinorVersionUpgrade is false. Engines that do not receive minor upgrades stay exposed to patched Redis/Memcached vulnerabilities.

aws.b.elasticache.in_transit.description: For ElastiCache replication groups, FAILs when TransitEncryptionEnabled is false. Client-to-node and replication traffic is then plaintext, so anyone on the network path can sniff cached data and AUTH tokens.

aws.b.elbv2.listener_presence.description: For Application and Network Load Balancers, FAILs when the completely collected listener inventory is empty. A load balancer without listeners serves no traffic and is usually an orphaned resource that still costs money and can be repurposed unnoticed.
aws.b.elbv2.listener_presence.pass_when: PASS when at least one listener exists.
aws.b.elbv2.listener_presence.fail_when: FAIL when the listener inventory was collected and is empty.

aws.b.elbv2.multiple_az.description: For Application, Network and Gateway Load Balancers, FAILs when fewer than two AvailabilityZones are declared. A single-zone ELBv2 is a single point of failure: an AZ outage takes the entry point down.
aws.b.elbv2.multiple_az.pass_when: PASS when two or more availability zones are attached.
aws.b.elbv2.multiple_az.fail_when: FAIL when fewer than two availability zones are attached.

aws.b.fsx.lustre_copy_backup_tags.description: For FSx file systems of type LUSTRE, FAILs when LustreConfiguration.CopyTagsToBackups is false. Backups without the file system's tags lose ownership/classification metadata and fall outside tag-based backup and access policies.
aws.b.fsx.lustre_copy_backup_tags.not_applicable_when: FileSystemType is WINDOWS, ONTAP or OPENZFS.

aws.b.fsx.netapp_ontap_multi_az.description: For FSx for NetApp ONTAP file systems, FAILs when OntapConfiguration.DeploymentType is not MULTI_AZ_1 or MULTI_AZ_2 (i.e. a single-AZ type). A single-AZ ONTAP deployment loses file service availability during an AZ outage.
aws.b.fsx.netapp_ontap_multi_az.pass_when: PASS when deploymentType is MULTI_AZ_1 or MULTI_AZ_2.
aws.b.fsx.netapp_ontap_multi_az.fail_when: FAIL when deploymentType is SINGLE_AZ_1 or SINGLE_AZ_2.

aws.b.fsx.openzfs_copy_backup_and_volume.description: For FSx OpenZFS file systems, FAILs unless both OpenZFSConfiguration.CopyTagsToBackups and CopyTagsToVolumes are true. Volumes and backups that do not inherit tags escape tag-based governance, cost allocation and ABAC policies.
aws.b.fsx.openzfs_copy_backup_and_volume.pass_when: PASS when both CopyTagsToBackups and CopyTagsToVolumes are true.
aws.b.fsx.openzfs_copy_backup_and_volume.fail_when: FAIL when either flag is false.

aws.b.fsx.openzfs_multi_az.description: For FSx OpenZFS file systems, FAILs when OpenZFSConfiguration.DeploymentType is anything other than MULTI_AZ_1 (for example SINGLE_AZ_1/2 or SINGLE_AZ_HA_1/2). Single-AZ deployments become unavailable if that availability zone fails.
aws.b.fsx.openzfs_multi_az.fail_when: FAIL when deploymentType is a single-AZ type.

aws.b.fsx.windows_multi_az.description: For FSx for Windows File Server, FAILs when WindowsConfiguration.DeploymentType is not MULTI_AZ_1. SINGLE_AZ_1 and SINGLE_AZ_2 shares become unavailable to SMB clients during an AZ failure.
aws.b.fsx.windows_multi_az.fail_when: FAIL when deploymentType is SINGLE_AZ_1 or SINGLE_AZ_2.

aws.b.inspector.admin_ec2_auto_enable.description: Scope-level check run only when the caller account is verified as the ENABLED Inspector delegated administrator: FAILs when the organization configuration's autoEnable.ec2 is false, so EC2 instance vulnerability scanning is not auto-enabled for member accounts. As a result new EC2 instances in member accounts are not scanned for OS/package CVEs and network reachability.
aws.b.inspector.admin_ec2_auto_enable.pass_when: PASS when the verified delegated administrator's autoEnable.ec2 is true.
aws.b.inspector.admin_ec2_auto_enable.fail_when: FAIL when the verified delegated administrator's autoEnable.ec2 is false.
aws.b.inspector.admin_ec2_auto_enable.not_applicable_when: No delegated administrator is configured, or the enabled delegated administrator is a different account (DENIED if the reads were denied).

aws.b.inspector.admin_ecr_auto_enable.description: Scope-level check run only when the caller account is verified as the ENABLED Inspector delegated administrator: FAILs when the organization configuration's autoEnable.ecr is false, so ECR container image scanning is not auto-enabled for member accounts. As a result images pushed to member-account ECR repositories are not scanned for vulnerabilities.
aws.b.inspector.admin_ecr_auto_enable.pass_when: PASS when the verified delegated administrator's autoEnable.ecr is true.
aws.b.inspector.admin_ecr_auto_enable.fail_when: FAIL when the verified delegated administrator's autoEnable.ecr is false.
aws.b.inspector.admin_ecr_auto_enable.not_applicable_when: No delegated administrator is configured, or the enabled delegated administrator is a different account (DENIED if the reads were denied).

aws.b.inspector.admin_lambda_auto_enable.description: Scope-level check run only when the caller account is verified as the ENABLED Inspector delegated administrator: FAILs when the organization configuration's autoEnable.lambda is false, so Lambda standard (dependency) scanning is not auto-enabled for member accounts.
